title: Fix the String Comparison
description: The program should check whether a user's input matches the word 'yes'.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 'Confirmed' since input's text is 'yes'.
actualProblem: == compares object references, not string content. Since input was built with new String("yes"), it is a distinct object from the literal "yes", so input == "yes" is false even though their text is identical, printing 'Not confirmed'.
explanation: To compare the actual text content of two String objects in Java, use .equals(), not ==. == only tells you whether both references point to the exact same object in memory, which is unreliable for strings created separately.
